# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 55 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 55 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_055_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 1 — The Parable of the Vineyard

**55:1** "Now listen to this parable, which has to do with fasting. A man owned a field and had many slaves. He planted a vineyard in one part of the field and put a reliable, well-regarded slave in charge of it as steward. He gave this slave one instruction: fence the vineyard in — nothing else — until I get back. Keep this one commandment and you'll have your freedom in my household."

**55:2** "The owner then went abroad. Once he was gone, the slave got to work and put up the fence around the vineyard. When the fencing was done, he noticed that the vineyard was overrun with weeds."

**55:3** "He thought it over: I've already done what my master told me to do. But I could also dig up this vineyard — and if I do, it'll be much more attractive. Free from weeds, it'll produce far more fruit without being strangled by them. So he dug the whole vineyard and pulled out every weed he could find. The vineyard became beautiful and thriving, no longer choked by weeds."

**55:4** "After some time the owner came back and went into the vineyard. He saw that it was perfectly fenced, and also dug, with every weed gone and the vine growing luxuriantly. He was thrilled with what the slave had done. He called his beloved son and his closest advisors and told them exactly what he had instructed the slave to do and what he had found the slave to have accomplished."

**55:5** "They all celebrated with the master because of the slave. The master said: I promised this slave his freedom if he kept my one commandment. He kept it — and beyond that, he did extraordinary work in the vineyard and made me very happy. Because of what he's done, I want to make him a co-heir with my son. When a good idea came to him, he didn't ignore it — he acted on it."

**55:6** "The master's son agreed: the slave deserved to be made a co-heir. A few days later the master threw a feast and sent the slave a large quantity of food from the celebration. The slave received the food from his master, took enough for himself, and shared the rest with his fellow slaves."

**55:7** "The other slaves were delighted with the food and began praying for him, asking that he would find even greater favor with the master, because of how generously he had treated them. The master heard all about this and was overjoyed at his slave's actions and the generosity behind them. He gathered his friends and his son and told them how the slave had shared the food he'd received. They were even more convinced that the slave fully deserved to share the inheritance with the son."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the narrative texture of the vineyard parable and its adoptionist christological implications.*
